about.title: Del Mar Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Del Mar draws visitors to its beaches, racetrack, and Camino Del Mar shops, which means property owners along these corridors and near Via De La Valle and Del Mar Heights Road have a duty to keep walkways, stairs, and parking areas reasonably safe. When a wet floor, broken pavement, poor lighting, or a hidden hazard causes a fall, the property owner may bear responsibility if they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the danger and did nothing to fix it or warn visitors. These cases often turn on evidence that disappears fast, like surveillance footage or maintenance logs. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects injured people in Del Mar with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, gather the right evidence, and explain your options under California's two-year filing window. There's no cost to get connected, and attorneys in this network work on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before It's Too Late

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help gather maintenance records, prior complaints, and inspection history that support this.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears
items.desc: Many Del Mar businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you were partly at fault, but your share of fault can lower what you're owed. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that fairly accounts for your role, if any.

items.question: I fell at a business near Camino Del Mar. Who is responsible?
items.answer: Responsibility usually falls on whoever controls the property, whether that's the business owner, a landlord, or a management company. It depends on who had a duty to maintain that specific area and whether they knew about the hazard. An independent attorney can help sort out which party, or parties, may be liable.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, though claims against a public entity, like a city-owned facility, have a much shorter notice deadline. Missing these windows can end your ability to recover. It's worth getting a timeline reviewed early.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for not seeing the hazard?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you share some responsibility, though your total recovery may be reduced by your percentage of fault. This makes it important to document the scene, photos, and any witnesses right away. An attorney can help present your side accurately.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything for connecting me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm. Attorneys in our network work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
